article_title: Anarchy & Community at Modern Times, 1851-1863
author: John Calvin Spurlock
page_locator: PDF pp. 17-18 of article file; printed pp. 45-46
evidence_type: historical secondary
exact_factual_observation: A retrospective account says residents informally refused trade and speech to people considered undesirable until they left.
what_source_establishes: The settlement used distributed ostracism as a non-state removal mechanism.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not document allegations, notice, appeal, proportionality, or the removed people's accounts.
author_interpretation: Informal community pressure substituted for formal government.
alternative_interpretation: The account may exaggerate coherence and is based on a late, hostile, pseudonymous source.
response_process: Collective refusal of economic and social contact.
outcome: Targets reportedly left; no later safety or reintegration outcome is recorded.
transferability: Useful mainly as a warning that separation power needs explicit procedure.
likely_article_destination: From visitor to member / a new discipline-and-separation section
notes: The cited 1870 account postdates the nominal 1851-1863 study period.

article_title: Anarchy & Community at Modern Times, 1851-1863
author: John Calvin Spurlock
evidence_type: historical secondary
exact_factual_observation: The same informal sanction was used against a woman whose dress and publicity offended local norms; she left.
what_source_establishes: A removal tool aimed at harmful conduct can also enforce conformity.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not establish that the woman posed a safety risk.
author_interpretation: The episode illustrates community standards operating without law.
alternative_interpretation: It may instead show gendered norm enforcement and reputational punishment.
response_process: Public criticism and social pressure.
outcome: Departure.
transferability: Any expulsion system needs a conduct threshold, protected nonconformity, and review.
likely_article_destination: From visitor to member / governance safeguards
notes: Relevant precisely because the target was not shown to be dangerous.

article_title: The Ashram of Graton Road: Morning Star Ranch, a California Commune in the 1960's
author: Jefferson P. Selth
evidence_type: participant-observer historical account
exact_factual_observation: An open-access rule and near-absence of resident rules coincided with a large nonworking transient population, serious sanitation failures, and incidents involving knives, guns, assault, and hepatitis.
what_source_establishes: Warmth and unrestricted entry did not supply a safety boundary or carrying-capacity control.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not isolate which governance change would have prevented each incident.
author_interpretation: The author treats principled openness and administrative incapacity as central to collapse.
alternative_interpretation: County hostility and code enforcement also materially shaped the ending.
response_process: Little internal screening or enforceable discipline; county legal and health processes became the operative boundary.
outcome: The county closed the settlement and structures were demolished.
transferability: High: admissions, minimum conduct, health capacity, and emergency authority must be designed together.
likely_article_destination: From visitor to member / math of absorption
notes: The current article already uses an open-door failure; this is an independent, concrete case.

article_title: The Brotherhood of the Sun, 1969-1985: A Memoir
author: Melanie Arcudi and Pauline Meyer
evidence_type: participant memoir with editorial framing
exact_factual_observation: A council remained subject to Norman Paulsen's approval while many members reportedly did not know about a weapons arsenal; the memoir also alleges substance misuse, unchecked spending, and arrests involving impaired driving and assault with a deadly weapon.
what_source_establishes: Nominal councils do not constrain a leader who controls information, security, and final approval.
what_source_does_not_establish: The memoir alone does not independently prove every allegation or establish criminal disposition.
author_interpretation: The authors present leader capture and secrecy as causes of decline.
alternative_interpretation: Some details may reflect a dissident faction's retrospective account.
response_process: Internal protest followed by expulsion; later litigation by former members.
outcome: Population fell sharply; property was sold; the lawsuit did not deliver a documented remedy.
transferability: High for structural warning; lower for individual allegations.
likely_article_destination: Founderism: the four questions
notes: Do not diagnose the leader; verify arrests, property, and litigation before publication.

article_title: The Brotherhood of the Sun, 1969-1985: A Memoir
author: Melanie Arcudi and Pauline Meyer
evidence_type: participant memoir
exact_factual_observation: Members who protested were reportedly expelled after eight to ten years without financial assistance and labeled traitors.
what_source_establishes: Exit can be formally available yet punitive when livelihood, equity, identity, and reputation are leader-controlled.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not provide a complete accounting of contributions or governing documents.
author_interpretation: The memoir treats the expulsions as retaliation and dispossession.
alternative_interpretation: The leadership's justification is not presented in comparable detail.
response_process: Leader-controlled removal and reputational labeling.
outcome: Departure without documented settlement; attempted group lawsuit failed.
transferability: High as a design question: separation must include neutral accounting, anti-retaliation, and appeal.
likely_article_destination: Money and land / exit terms
notes: Pair with independent records before naming specific alleged wrongdoing in the article.

article_title: Darkness into Light: Laurence Oliphant's Experience of Communal Discipline in the United States & Palestine
author: Anne Taylor
community_group: Brotherhood of the New Life / Thomas Lake Harris
evidence_type: archival biography
exact_factual_observation: Harris claimed unusual access to followers' thoughts and used humiliation, isolation, exhausting labor, food and sleep deprivation, and alleged beatings; Oliphant remained for more than a decade before outside family support helped him leave.
what_source_establishes: Spiritualized surveillance plus deprivation can disable internal resistance, and ordinary outside ties can become exit infrastructure.
what_source_does_not_establish: The article does not supply a comparative sample or a formal intervention evaluation.
author_interpretation: Taylor describes a progression from enchantment to domination and escape.
alternative_interpretation: A follower might have described some practices as voluntary discipline, but the deprivation and violence claims undermine meaningful consent.
response_process: Personal domination; eventual support from wife and family rather than an internal remedy.
outcome: Oliphant exited and publicly broke with Harris.
transferability: High for non-waivable rights and protected external contact.
likely_article_destination: Founderism / a new non-waivable rights safeguard
notes: Verify the most serious abuse and suicide claims in Taylor's underlying biography before publication.

article_title: Redemptory Intimacy: The Family Culture of the Unification Church
author: Arthur S. Parsons
evidence_type: participant observation and interviews
exact_factual_observation: Personal disclosure and confession were routed upward to central figures; members were pressured to confess disapproved feelings, while acceptance and emotional uplift followed compliance.
what_source_establishes: A practice can feel intimate and therapeutic while supplying information and leverage to a hierarchy.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not measure long-term clinical benefit or compare participants with nonparticipants.
author_interpretation: Parsons argues that emotional intimacy organizes personalized social control.
alternative_interpretation: Participants may have experienced genuine support alongside control; the two are not mutually exclusive.
response_process: Disclosure, correction by superiors, and conditional approval.
outcome: The article documents obedience and solidarity, not an independent safety or recovery outcome.
transferability: High: care data should be confidential and structurally separated from sanctions and membership decisions.
likely_article_destination: Peer counseling / the four domains
notes: Mechanism is more transferable than the paper's broad characterization of members.

article_title: Redemptory Intimacy: The Family Culture of the Unification Church
author: Arthur S. Parsons
evidence_type: participant observation and interviews
exact_factual_observation: Rules were displaced by personalized accountability to spiritual superiors; aggression was redirected inward as personal failure or outward toward the secular world.
what_source_establishes: Distributed emotional practice is not by itself distributed authority; informal personalism can be more controlling than explicit rules.
what_source_does_not_establish: The article does not show that all intimate practice has this effect.
author_interpretation: The author concludes that intimacy in this case thrives on authoritarian personalism.
alternative_interpretation: The mechanism depends on hierarchy, compulsory disclosure, and fused roles, not intimacy alone.
response_process: Correction through personal superiors rather than impersonal rights or review.
outcome: High solidarity and self-sacrifice; no demonstrated independent remedy for abuse of authority.
transferability: High if framed as a firewall requirement, not an indictment of peer counseling.
likely_article_destination: The four domains / community as therapist
notes: Direct challenge to treating healing capacity as sufficient protection against capture.

article_title: The Status and Self-Perception of Women in the Oneida Community
author: Ellen Wayland-Smith
evidence_type: archival analysis of private letters and diaries
exact_factual_observation: The author finds roughly equal male and female status but also shared submission to Noyes, whose authority was fused with divine authority; later letters describe pressure and regret.
what_source_establishes: Horizontal equality can coexist with vertical domination, so within-group parity is an incomplete freedom test.
what_source_does_not_establish: The study closely analyzes only a few writers and emphasizes the breakup period.
author_interpretation: Dependence on Noyes's mediated will limited broader liberation.
alternative_interpretation: Members also described genuine connection and benefits; retrospective regret did not make every aspect coercive.
response_process: Mutual criticism and leader-defined spiritual obedience.
outcome: Community cohesion weakened as members began interpreting belief independently; the community later broke up.
transferability: High as an evaluation lens: ask who can define reality, not only who is equal to peers.
likely_article_destination: Founderism / success criteria
notes: The paper's gender theory is dated; the archival power evidence remains useful.

article_title: Donald Vose: Home Grown Traitor
author: Anitra Balzer
evidence_type: historical biography
exact_factual_observation: Vose informed investigators in a case arising from the 1910 Los Angeles Times bombing and was subsequently framed by former associates as a traitor and ostracized.
what_source_establishes: A community's harmful-person label can be inverted against an informer or dissident.
what_source_does_not_establish: The article does not neutrally establish Vose's motives or every disputed event.
author_interpretation: Balzer presents Vose as a morally compromised traitor.
alternative_interpretation: The same record can be read as a warning about loyalty norms punishing external reporting.
response_process: Reputational condemnation and social exclusion.
outcome: Vose testified; the defendants were convicted; he remained estranged from the community.
transferability: High for protected reporting; low for conclusions about Vose's character.
likely_article_destination: Governance safeguards / external reporting
notes: Use as a framing caution, not a heroic or villainous biography.

article_title: Jonestown and Bishop Hill: Continuities and Disjunctures in Religious Conflict
author: John R. Hall
evidence_type: comparative historical interpretation
exact_factual_observation: Both cases involved escalating conflict with defectors, relatives, custody claims, and outside authorities; the paper notes that children at Jonestown did not knowingly consent and that some adults were coerced.
what_source_establishes: External-contact and child-custody conflicts can become siege triggers when no trusted interface or appeal exists.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not show that outside intervention caused the underlying coercion or that a protocol would have prevented escalation.
author_interpretation: Hall gives substantial causal weight to sect-opponent conflict and apocalyptic framing.
alternative_interpretation: The comparison risks over-symmetrizing leaders, coerced residents, relatives, and officials.
response_process: Ad hoc confrontation among leaders, relatives, courts, media, and officials.
outcome: Murder-suicide at Jonestown; assassination and later institutional dissolution at Bishop Hill.
transferability: Moderate: design trusted escalation and visitor/custody procedures before crisis.
likely_article_destination: Children / legal coupling / external oversight
notes: Any publication use needs more balanced Jonestown sources.

article_title: The Use of Structural Arrangements and Organizational Strategies by Urban Communes
author: William L. Smith
evidence_type: small comparative questionnaire study
exact_factual_observation: The study codes confession, mutual criticism, sanctions, reprimands, rules, trial membership, hierarchy, and permanent expulsion as commitment mechanisms but gives almost no case-level process or outcome detail.
what_source_establishes: A research tradition measured structures associated with commitment while leaving fairness and safety outcomes largely unobserved.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not establish that any listed mechanism caused survival, safety, or harm.
author_interpretation: The author explores Kanter-style commitment mechanisms and calls for a larger study.
alternative_interpretation: Gatekeeper-selected respondents and self-report may make high-control structures look orderly.
response_process: Varied sanctions and expulsions, details mostly absent.
outcome: No traceable post-intervention outcomes.
transferability: High as a research-gap finding; low as evidence for any particular rule.
likely_article_destination: Research/school function / success criteria
notes: A useful null about what the journal literature records.

article_title: Foreign Volunteers in the Kibbutz: The Dilemma of Ideology vs. The Work Force
author: Shalom Endleman
evidence_type: six-month participant observation plus interviews and newspaper material
exact_factual_observation: Temporary volunteers lacked access to formal decision-making and said they were blamed for drug use and other youth misconduct that members were reluctant to identify or punish internally.
what_source_establishes: A low-voice outsider group can become the default suspect when internal accountability is weak.
what_source_does_not_establish: The article does not adjudicate the underlying drug allegations case by case.
author_interpretation: Mutual distrust followed a deteriorating labor exchange.
alternative_interpretation: Members also raised real boundary and child-influence concerns; scapegoating and genuine risk may coexist.
response_process: Complaints among volunteers, increased segregation, stay limits, screening, orientation, and in three cases program termination.
outcome: No formal grievance outcome; some programs ended.
transferability: High: temporary residents need conduct rules, voice, grievance access, and evidence-based attribution.
likely_article_destination: Membership pipeline / governance safeguards
notes: Avoid treating either volunteers' or members' allegations as fully verified.

article_title: Success in Intentional Communities: The Problem of Evaluation
author: Jonathan Wagner
evidence_type: conceptual and literature review
exact_factual_observation: Wagner separates goal attainment, social merit, longevity, size, cohesion, influence, and personal growth and shows that the criteria can conflict.
what_source_establishes: Success is a vector of named outcomes, not one verdict.
what_source_does_not_establish: The paper does not validate a modern measurement instrument.
author_interpretation: Ambiguous criteria let analysts reach nearly any preferred conclusion.
alternative_interpretation: A shorter dashboard could preserve the insight without importing all seven criteria.
response_process: Not applicable.
outcome: Methodological outcome: evaluation claims become criterion-specific.
transferability: Very high for article framing.
likely_article_destination: Why communities fail / plan the funeral
notes: Use specific outcome terms rather than success or failure alone.

article_title: Success in Intentional Communities: The Problem of Evaluation
author: Jonathan Wagner
evidence_type: conceptual and literature review
exact_factual_observation: The paper warns that cohesion and member-reported fulfillment can rate authoritarian groups highly and can conceal planned exit or harm.
what_source_establishes: Cohesion, testimony, and longevity are not safety proxies.
what_source_does_not_establish: The examples do not quantify how often such false positives occur.
author_interpretation: Evaluation must name the value being measured.
alternative_interpretation: Cohesion remains a legitimate outcome if separately reported and not moralized.
response_process: Not applicable.
outcome: A group may look cohesive while suppressing autonomy or safety.
transferability: Very high for an explicit evaluation safeguard.
likely_article_destination: Founderism / community as therapist / success criteria
notes: Directly complicates the article's reliance on observable flourishing and relational vitality.

article_title: Intergenerational Discontinuity in the Israeli Kibbutz
author: Jack Quarter
evidence_type: participant observation interviews and small surveys
exact_factual_observation: Time-away and return policies reduced insecurity, supported exploration, and preserved a route home; former-member stigma had also declined.
what_source_establishes: An outward door works better when it includes a reversible moratorium and dignified reintegration.
what_source_does_not_establish: The study is limited to two kibbutzim and cannot isolate causal effects.
author_interpretation: Modernization creates both autonomy and retention tension.
alternative_interpretation: Easy return may increase short-term departure while reducing permanent rupture.
response_process: Authorized time away, family support, and return eligibility.
outcome: Substantial departure; some return; later education, work, and partners can make return harder.
transferability: High for exit and alumni design.
likely_article_destination: What the children will say / plan the funeral
notes: Do not treat retention as the only desired outcome.

article_title: Intergenerational Discontinuity in the Israeli Kibbutz
author: Jack Quarter
evidence_type: participant observation interviews and small surveys
exact_factual_observation: The comprehensive child peer group supplied independence and support but could also be harsh toward individual children.
what_source_establishes: Collective childrearing shifts some power from parents to peers; the peer group itself needs safeguarding.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not document a persistently dangerous child or evaluate a protection protocol.
author_interpretation: Peer centrality is both a resource and a cost.
alternative_interpretation: The harshness may vary by cohort and institutional design.
response_process: No specific case response is documented.
outcome: No traceable child-safety outcome.
transferability: Moderate: add adult oversight, confidential reporting, and options outside a single peer cohort.
likely_article_destination: What the children will say about you
notes: Adjacent, not responsive to the dangerous-child question.

article_title: The Kibbutz as an Alternative Living Community and the Role of Education
author: Maria Folling-Albers
evidence_type: historical and educational analysis
exact_factual_observation: The author argues that voluntary adult membership requires professional training adequate for life outside the kibbutz; earlier expectations had burdened departures with guilt.
what_source_establishes: Exit is not fully voluntary if a community-raised young adult lacks portable livelihood capacity.
what_source_does_not_establish: The article does not compare specific credential programs or later earnings.
author_interpretation: Education must enable a real choice for or against membership.
alternative_interpretation: Portable capability may also increase attrition while making retained membership more voluntary.
response_process: Professional training plus an explicit adult choice.
outcome: About half of youth were reported to apply for membership; individual outcomes are not followed.
transferability: High for child and exit design.
likely_article_destination: What the children will say about you
notes: Adds material capability to the article's moral permission to leave.

article_title: A Workshop for the Education and Formation of Communal Households
author: Ronda Heard and Susan Berger
evidence_type: program report by facilitators
exact_factual_observation: Households formed through a premove workshop were described as more stable, responsible, and crisis-resistant than rapid or advertisement-based placements; workshops used values comparison, conflict practice, consensus training, and group simulation.
what_source_establishes: Selection improves when prospective members practice together under realistic conditions before co-residence.
what_source_does_not_establish: No controlled comparison, denominator, or statistical test is supplied.
author_interpretation: The facilitators attribute better functioning to preparation and group formation.
alternative_interpretation: Facilitator enthusiasm and selection effects may explain part of the difference.
response_process: Originally 40 hours, later shortened; real exercises and core-group formation.
outcome: Described as fewer crises and greater stability.
transferability: Moderate; suitable as a candidate design, not a proven effect size.
likely_article_destination: From visitor to member
notes: The article's exercises involving disclosure also need privacy boundaries.

article_title: A Workshop for the Education and Formation of Communal Households
author: Ronda Heard and Susan Berger
evidence_type: program report by facilitators
exact_factual_observation: Outside mediators were underused because residents distrusted them, leading the program to build the mediator relationship when a house formed rather than after crisis.
what_source_establishes: Independent help is more usable if legitimacy and familiarity exist before conflict.
what_source_does_not_establish: The paper does not quantify mediation uptake or effectiveness after the policy change.
author_interpretation: Early relationship-building should reduce resistance to outside help.
alternative_interpretation: A mediator may still be distrusted or conflicted unless selection and confidentiality are explicit.
response_process: Pre-established circuit-rider relationship.
outcome: No measured outcome yet reported.
transferability: High as a low-cost design principle; evidence strength is moderate.
likely_article_destination: Membership pipeline / conflict architecture
notes: Pairs with an independent appeal channel rather than replacing it.

article_title: The Contributions of Accounting to the Early Success of the Harmonists
author: Tonya K. Flesher and Dale L. Flesher
community_group: Harmony Society, New Harmony, Shakers, Oneida
evidence_type: archival accounting history
exact_factual_observation: The Harmony articles specified withdrawal refunds and service-based payments; several communities used budgets and departmental accounts, while trust without internal controls enabled hidden funds, losses, and failed legal proof.
what_source_establishes: Accounting, internal control, and exit valuation are governance safeguards, not merely business administration.
what_source_does_not_establish: Recordkeeping alone does not prevent leader capture or prove overall success.
author_interpretation: Sophisticated managerial accounting contributed to organizational capacity; weak controls created avoidable losses.
alternative_interpretation: The same accounting system can also intensify surveillance unless member rights govern its use.
response_process: Budgets, recurring reports, inventories, refund rules, and internal controls.
outcome: Improved management in some cases; material loss and costly litigation where records were absent.
transferability: High for operational design.
likely_article_destination: Money and land / founderism
notes: Especially relevant to community-held property and member equity.

article_title: The Rise and Fall of Utopia: The Oneida Community Crises of 1852 and 1879
author: Lawrence Foster
evidence_type: historical synthesis
exact_factual_observation: After leadership, value, and sexual-status crises, Oneida ended complex marriage and converted to a joint-stock form after consultation, with provisions concerning children.
what_source_establishes: Institutional transformation can preserve assets and relationships when the original form ends.
what_source_does_not_establish: The paper is comparatively sympathetic and does not resolve coercion in Oneida's sexual hierarchy.
author_interpretation: Foster interprets the transition as adaptation rather than simple failure.
alternative_interpretation: The transition can be both adaptive and a response to accumulated domination and conflict.
response_process: Consultation, rule change, and legal-economic conversion.
outcome: The communal form ended; a successor enterprise continued.
transferability: High for succession and dissolution planning; use a more balanced source for sexual governance.
likely_article_destination: Plan the funeral at the wedding
notes: Supports an existing article idea with a historical mechanism.

article_title: Intercommunal Relationships among Nineteenth-century Communal Societies in America
author: Otohiko Okugawa
evidence_type: historical database analysis
exact_factual_observation: Members, practices, and personnel frequently moved among communities at founding, during operation, and after dissolution; many residents of dissolved groups joined other communal efforts.
what_source_establishes: Movement-level continuity can exceed the lifespan of any single institution.
what_source_does_not_establish: The database's completeness and coding reliability are not independently evaluated here.
author_interpretation: Intercommunal relationships are central to understanding communal vitality.
alternative_interpretation: Migration may reflect individual survival rather than intentional federation.
response_process: Branching, schism, relocation, imitation, and member migration.
outcome: Ideas and members persisted across organizational deaths.
transferability: High for alumni, fork, and federation design.
likely_article_destination: Founderism / plan the funeral
notes: Sharpens the article's existing fork idea with movement-level evidence.

article_title: Communes & the Outside World: Seclusion & Involvement
author: Yaacov Oved
evidence_type: historical comparison
exact_factual_observation: Even separatist communities depended on markets, law, neighbors, and visitors; remote socialist colonies often spent their energy on subsistence, lost skilled members, and failed to influence wider society.
what_source_establishes: External coupling is unavoidable, and cheap remoteness can reverse a movement's intended mission.
what_source_does_not_establish: The comparison is selective and does not specify an optimal degree of separation.
author_interpretation: Viable groups find context-specific combinations of detachment and involvement.
alternative_interpretation: Remote survival may be the intended goal for some communities rather than a failure.
response_process: Trade, legal compliance, neighbor relations, tourism, and labor mobility.
outcome: Some remote change-oriented colonies became isolated and fragile.
transferability: High for a coupling and site-selection matrix.
likely_article_destination: Selecting your couplings / a note on Africa
notes: Avoid treating seclusion and involvement as one linear scale.

article_title: Job Harriman and Llano del Rio: The Chimerical Quest for a Secular Utopia
author: Knox Mellon
evidence_type: historical synthesis using minutes and correspondence
exact_factual_observation: Llano admitted more people than its water, soil, food, and agricultural skill base could support; leadership conflict and debt compounded the ecological error, while dissidents included both low contributors and highly skilled hard workers.
what_source_establishes: Values fit and personal need ratios cannot substitute for site carrying capacity, capability mix, or fair treatment of dissent.
what_source_does_not_establish: Conflicting participant testimony prevents a simple causal ranking.
author_interpretation: The author attributes failure to environmental, financial, political, and human factors.
alternative_interpretation: Some complaints may reflect factional struggle, but labeling all critics as lazy is unsupported.
response_process: Commission disputes, resignations, departures, and eventual relocation attempts.
outcome: Population collapsed; the California colony failed.
transferability: High for intake math and dissent safeguards.
likely_article_destination: Math of absorption / founderism
notes: Strong complication of moralized member categories.

article_title: The Utopian Project in a Communal Experiment of the 1930's: The Sunrise Colony in Historical and Comparative Perspective
author: Francis Shor
evidence_type: historical comparison
exact_factual_observation: Recruitment downplayed debt and swampy land; screening did not resolve heterogeneous aims, farming-skill gaps, and labor conflict; work rules and fines followed, and debt plus weak farm prices helped end the project.
what_source_establishes: Recruitment truthfulness, task capability, site economics, and labor governance belong in the membership pipeline.
what_source_does_not_establish: The paper does not isolate the effect of screening from the Depression-era economy.
author_interpretation: The author emphasizes the interaction of utopian aspiration with material and political conditions.
alternative_interpretation: Government support and market changes, not only internal design, shaped survival.
response_process: Screening, labor managers/boards, work-day rules, and fines.
outcome: Persistent conflict and eventual failure after economic support weakened.
transferability: High for pre-purchase and pre-admission checks.
likely_article_destination: Choose by values / math of absorption / money and land
notes: Values agreement is necessary but not sufficient.

article_title: The Decline of the Shakers: Evidence from the United States Census
author: William Sims Bainbridge
evidence_type: census linkage and historical records
exact_factual_observation: Many children entered with disrupted families; retention was low, especially among young males, and the communities functioned partly as refuges while bearing education and care obligations.
what_source_establishes: A community that admits vulnerable families can become a de facto care institution whether or not it planned to.
what_source_does_not_establish: Surname and census inference cannot reconstruct each child's welfare or reasons for leaving.
author_interpretation: Recruitment failed to offset defection and mortality.
alternative_interpretation: Low retention may represent successful temporary refuge rather than failed childrearing.
response_process: Long-term residence, schooling, and religious socialization; individual interventions are not described.
outcome: Most entrants did not remain for life.
transferability: Moderate: capacity planning must include care duties and transition support.
likely_article_destination: Math of absorption / children
notes: Adjacent to, not a direct dangerous-child case.

article_title: Foreign Volunteers in the Kibbutz: The Dilemma of Ideology vs. The Work Force
author: Shalom Endleman
evidence_type: six-month participant observation plus interviews and newspaper material
exact_factual_observation: Volunteers supplied about 7.3 percent of work hours but remained segregated, transient, low-voice workers doing undesirable jobs; both members and volunteers came to perceive exploitation.
what_source_establishes: An egalitarian member economy can externalize hierarchy onto volunteers or nonmembers.
what_source_does_not_establish: The percentage and marriage counts rely partly on contemporaneous institutional and newspaper sources.
author_interpretation: A structural labor shortage transformed an ideological exchange into a class boundary.
alternative_interpretation: Temporary work can be mutually beneficial if terms, voice, learning, and duration are genuinely fair.
response_process: Shorter workdays and material support alongside social separation; later screening, orientation, automation, or program closure.
outcome: Continued labor dependence with alienation; three kibbutzim ended programs by 1986.
transferability: High for role, voice, compensation, and grievance design for nonmembers.
likely_article_destination: Labor and membership architecture
notes: A major unexpected Track B finding.

article_title: Utopia and Reality: Some Contradictions and Challenges in Kibbutz Education
author: Dov Darom
evidence_type: educational essay with cited statistics
exact_factual_observation: Children noticed the gap between professed ideals and ordinary practice; the author argues for explicit value education that also protects a student's right to reject community values.
what_source_establishes: A community school needs institutional honesty about failures and an explicit right to dissent, not indoctrination or value-neutrality.
what_source_does_not_establish: The essay does not evaluate a specific curriculum or long-term child outcomes.
author_interpretation: Utopia and reality must be taught as a productive tension.
alternative_interpretation: The framework may understate power differences between educator and community-raised child.
response_process: Explicit discussion, behavioral modeling, and protected disagreement.
outcome: No measured outcome; roughly half of kibbutz-born youth were said to leave.
transferability: Moderate to high for educational governance.
likely_article_destination: What the children will say / internal school-research function
notes: The article's present child audit is retrospective; this adds an in-process right to disagree.

article_title: The Rajneesh Experience: A Report
author: Louis C. Androes
evidence_type: first-person descriptive report
exact_factual_observation: The report portrays free exit, changing elected leadership, and little coercion; an editorial note states it was written before the leader's arrest and deportation and publishes it as a first-hand document rather than an authoritative assessment.
what_source_establishes: Access-rich or participant-adjacent observation can miss concealed or later-emerging harm.
what_source_does_not_establish: This article by itself does not establish which claims were false when written.
author_interpretation: The author viewed work-as-worship and leadership favorably, with only a mild warning about dogma.
alternative_interpretation: The report's incompleteness may reflect timing and access rather than bad faith.
response_process: No documented internal correction process.
outcome: Later events overtook the snapshot; the article does not analyze them.
transferability: High as a source-audit rule; low as substantive governance evidence.
likely_article_destination: Research method / source cautions
notes: Do not use its favorable claims as confirmed facts.

article_title: Cumulative targeted search and issue-by-issue discovery scan
author: Research checkpoint

exact_factual_observation: The article says the mid-1980s economic crisis strengthened rather than weakened technocrats even though it marked a major failure of economic leadership; unhappy rank-and-file members accepted greater dependence on those expected to lead them out of crisis. article_title: Pensions on the Kibbutz: The Implications of the Undermining of Social Security for the Aged in Communal Societies
author: John Gal
evidence_type: historical policy analysis with movement records and survey evidence
exact_factual_observation: Most members mistook collective provident funds for pensions; after withdrawals during crisis, the depleted funds dissolved and merged with commercial-bank funds. At Beit Oren, advisers reportedly told elderly members the kibbutz could not provide for them and advised them to leave, though the wording was disputed. Within five years 43 percent of kibbutzim had joined pension funds and 68 percent of the rest planned to; individual pension rights persisted if a member left.
what_source_establishes: A pooled communal promise can fail precisely when vulnerable members need it, while portable individual entitlements remain usable across exit and institutional crisis.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not show that all elderly members were abandoned, settle the disputed wording at Beit Oren, or compare long-term outcomes under each pension arrangement.
author_interpretation: The author argues that aging, economic crisis, and weakened collective values undermined perceived security and made pensions a response to future uncertainty.
alternative_interpretation: The movement continued caring for many elderly members, and individualization can also weaken communal solidarity or distribute market risk.
response_process: Public controversy, movement debate, legal-economic advice, and voluntary entry into individual pension funds followed the crisis.
outcome: The collective funds disappeared; the Beit Oren episode changed movement debate, and individual pension adoption spread quickly but unevenly.
transferability: High for portable vested benefits, transparent benefit language, reserves, and protection of elderly or dependent members on exit.
likely_article_destination: Money and land / fair separation / vulnerable-member security
notes: Attribute the disputed Beit Oren instruction precisely. DOI: https://doi.org/10.9707/0739-1250.1782

article_title: So Much They Have Got for Their Folly: Shaker Apostates and the Tale of Woe
author: Elizabeth A. DeWolfe

likely_article_destination: Dissent and external reporting / alumni feedback / founderism
notes: Treat reported apostate fates as narratives, not verified outcomes. DOI: https://doi.org/10.9707/0739-1250.1783

article_title: The Medium of Grace: Mutual Criticism in the Oneida Community
author: Tara McCarthy
page_locator: PDF pp. 4 and 9-12; printed pp. 94 and 99-102
evidence_type: historical synthesis drawing heavily on Oneida publications and memoirs
exact_factual_observation: Mutual Criticism was usually volunteered but could be mandated in extreme cases. what_source_establishes: A community-wide grievance and discipline practice can offer broad participation while denying the subject a contemporaneous right of reply and extending conformity control to outside relationships.

alternative_interpretation: Rotating committees, cautions against grudges, and efforts to balance praise and reproof may have limited some misuse.
response_process: A standing or specially chosen committee delivered judgments; the subject was passive, and the article describes no independent appeal or recusal right.

article_title: The Medium of Grace: Mutual Criticism in the Oneida Community
author: Tara McCarthy
evidence_type: historical synthesis drawing on Oneida health claims and records
exact_factual_observation: Oneida used Mutual Criticism for minor ailments and serious disease. During an 1863-1864 diphtheria outbreak, several people died before a physician was called; after members said he disrespected Christ, he was dismissed. Noyes rejected doctors and drugs, said he would remain loyal to faith even if half died, and prescribed criticism and ice. The source reports five deaths among sixty cases and no deaths after that regimen began.
what_source_establishes: A peer-spiritual practice can become a substitute for independent medical care when the same leader controls both doctrine and access to clinicians.
what_source_does_not_establish: The sequence does not prove criticism or ice cured diphtheria, establish the counterfactual mortality under medical care, or supply a safe modern treatment model.
author_interpretation: The author treats criticism as a therapeutic as well as control mechanism and reports Community members' cure testimony.
alternative_interpretation: Nineteenth-century medicine was itself limited, and epidemic timing or ordinary recovery may explain the reported decline in deaths.
response_process: A physician was called late and then dismissed; leader-directed faith practice replaced him, with no independent medical decision authority described.
outcome: Five fatalities were recorded; the Community attributed later survival to criticism and ice, but the source cannot establish causation.
transferability: High for non-waivable medical access and independent clinical authority; zero for adopting the historical treatment.
likely_article_destination: Medicine / non-waivable rights / selecting legal couplings
notes: Historical health testimony is not clinical efficacy evidence. DOI: https://doi.org/10.9707/0739-1250.1788

article_title: Taking Shelter from the Coming Storm: The Millenial Impulse of the Church Universal and Triumphant's Royal Teton Ranch
author: Brad Whitsel
community_group: Church Universal and Triumphant / Royal Teton Ranch
page_locator: PDF pp. 3-4 and 17-18; printed pp. 2-3 and 16-17

likely_article_destination: Founderism / dissent / success and safety criteria

article_title: Communal Groups: Social Laboratories or Places of Exile?
author: Peter Michael Forster and William James Metcalf

article_title: Analyzing Communal Life-Spans: A Dynamic Structural Approach
author: James A. Kitts
page_locator: PDF pp. 3-5 and 9-10; printed pp. 14-16 and 20-21
evidence_type: comparative methodological synthesis and exploratory quantitative study
exact_factual_observation: Prior work treated longevity as an indicator of a well-functioning group even though commitment mechanisms can promote retention and conformity through renounced outside ties, monitoring, and sanctions. In an exploratory study of 408 American communities, centralization of power was positively related to survival in 1990-1995, while social density reduced survival probability; other structural studies produced context-dependent or reversed results.

alternative_interpretation: Centralization can improve coordination and exclusion can address genuine free-riding; short life can also reflect hostile context rather than failure.

transferability: High as a measurement rule: report safety, autonomy, exit, and correction separately from longevity and cohesion.

article_title: The Commune That Didn't Come to Town: The Love Israel Family and a Small Town in Idaho
author: Charles P. LeWarne

article_title: Just to Breathe: Personal Recollections of Synanon Founder Chuck Dederich
author: Ellen Broslovsky
page_locator: PDF pp. 2, 6, 10, and 13; printed pp. 97, 101, 105, and 108
evidence_type: insider retrospective memoir with an editorial introduction
exact_factual_observation: The editor says Synanon gave tremendous power to Dederich and handpicked associates and links this to violent actions and radical innovations in 1976-1978. outcome: The main institution ended after collapse and a later tax case; the Berlin branch survived at the article's date, while the memoir does not isolate causal effects.
transferability: High for testing founder exceptions, protecting sleep, separating therapy from governance, and giving branches a lawful refusal or fork path.

notes: Insider retrospective plus editor framing; verify violence, policy chronology, and Berlin outcome independently before article use. DOI: https://doi.org/10.9707/0739-1250.1620

article_title: Etienne Cabet: Icaria's Paradoxical ‘Papa’
author: Robert P. Sutton

After a later school confrontation frightened children and drew townspeople's attention, outsiders called the sheriff, who restored order. The majority subsequently voted to expel Cabet and his supporters, listed charges publicly, and the factions separated amid food, clothing, equity, and dissolution disputes.
what_source_establishes: A founder challenge reached an effective boundary only after factional violence, outside law enforcement, collective expulsion, and physical separation; delayed correction endangered people and communal assets.

article_title: The Male Work Ethic Was Busted: Black Bear Ranch, 1968-1974
author: Tim Hodgdon
page_locator: PDF pp. 11 and 13-14; printed pp. 104 and 106-107
evidence_type: historical analysis using interviews, participant writings, and archival material
exact_factual_observation: During a coercive anti-monogamy campaign, some members ignored the rule or complied only outwardly. General redefinition proceeded through what an insider called group decision-making and bullying in which the loudest faction often prevailed. Later, separate women's meetings built enough solidarity for women to challenge gendered labor; their organized pressure increased men's household work and changed some attitudes.
what_source_establishes: Consensus-like whole-group processes can hide bullying and false compliance, while an autonomous affinity channel can give a subordinated group enough backing to correct a normalized harm.

article_title: Dating and Educational Behaviors of Hutterian Youth

article_title: The Society of Separatists of Zoar vs....: Zoar and the Courts
author: Kathleen M. Fernandez
evidence_type: historical legal synthesis using articles of agreement, notices, testimony, and reported court decisions
exact_factual_observation: Zoar's articles assigned disputes to a five-member Standing Committee and stripped a dissatisfied member of further membership rights. After reports of tavern drunkenness, fighting, secret money, and hoarded goods, Johannes Goesele refused the committee hearing and remained in the tavern. Counsel then issued a conduct-specific eviction notice inviting excuse, extenuation, and cause against expulsion. Goesele sued instead. Courts upheld the communal contract under which separation or expulsion ended property claims; his wife could receive support only by returning to live and work at Zoar. The Society later gave the impoverished former members supplies.

response_process: Standing Committee jurisdiction; allegations and testimony; offered hearing; conduct-specific notice and opportunity to show cause; expulsion and eviction; external litigation; conditional support and later supplies. No neutral internal appeal is described.

article_title: Easter, 1832: A Brief Interlude of Peace for Georg Rapp's Harmony Society
author: Eileen Aiken English
community_group: Harmony Society and New Philadelphia seceders
evidence_type: historical reconstruction from conflicting community accounts, depositions, correspondence, and press material
exact_factual_observation: The Harmony Society and 1832 seceders agreed to a $105,000 separation payment in three installments with deductions and release conditions. The first payment was reduced and later adjusted; the final payment was delayed while the payer demanded release of claims. With the splinter settlement in debt and short of food and medicine, a delegation of 79 men arrived to present an appeal and seek asset records. Accounts disagree about weapons and who initiated violence. The militia intervened and a trial was scheduled, but the splinter society dissolved and the trial never occurred.

Without a neutral accounting and escalation channel, urgent material need and mixed-purpose collective action can turn an equity dispute into a safety crisis.

likely_article_destination: Fair separation / money and land / conflict architecture
notes: The source explicitly reconstructs incompatible accounts; do not choose a culprit where it does not. DOI: https://doi.org/10.9707/0739-1250.1487

article_title: Changing Pilots in Mid-Stream: How German-American Communitarian Societies Successfully Handled the Deaths of Their Founders
author: Michael Taylor
evidence_type: comparative historical synthesis
exact_factual_observation: George Rapp made no succession provision. A democratically elected Council of Elders, created during an earlier legal crisis with limited temporal authority, became the Society's religious and secular governing body after his death. When designated religious leader Jacob Henrici tried to establish absolute authority, the council and co-trustee R. L. Baker rebuked him. Henrici accepted the rebuke and remained minister; the community survived the transition for decades.
what_source_establishes: A representative body created before a succession crisis can become a practical override: it constrained a would-be autocrat without requiring either submission or total removal, and separated ministry from final governance.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not show how inclusive the election was, whether the council could handle abuse allegations, how often it checked leaders, or that the later society was otherwise democratic or safe.
author_interpretation: The author credits shared goals and the expanded Council of Elders with allowing the Society to survive its initial leadership transition.
alternative_interpretation: Henrici's willingness to accept correction and the community's continuity of purpose may have mattered as much as the council's formal design.
response_process: Preexisting elected council; post-founder expansion of authority; collective rebuke of successor; successor accepts limited role and remains in office.
outcome: The attempted concentration of power was checked and the Society continued for decades.
transferability: High for installing an elected, independently legitimate body before succession and giving it power to narrow a leader's role without making every correction existential.
likely_article_destination: Founderism / succession / tested override
notes: A positive mechanism, not proof that the council was adequate in all domains. DOI: https://doi.org/10.9707/0739-1250.1493

article_title: Changing Pilots in Mid-Stream: How German-American Communitarian Societies Successfully Handled the Deaths of Their Founders
author: Michael Taylor
evidence_type: comparative historical synthesis
exact_factual_observation: An 1854 inspired testimony attributed to Christian Metz condemned any dissolution of communal ties and threatened deprivation and disgrace for those responsible. In 1919, older members who remembered the testimony rejected a constitutional revision permitting reorganization or dissolution. In 1932, the Great Change separated the religious and business sides, allowing economic reorganization while preserving the church's stated spiritual purpose.

alternative_interpretation: Economic pressures and generational change may have driven both the delayed resistance and eventual reorganization more than institutional design did.
response_process: Archived prophetic prohibition; failed constitutional revision; later separation of religious and business institutions.
outcome: Reorganization was delayed in 1919 and achieved in 1932 without dissolving the religious body.
transferability: High for testing whether amendment rules bind founding texts and for considering separable legal entities when mission and operating form must change at different speeds.
likely_article_destination: Founderism / rule revision / plan the funeral
notes: The source discusses inherited veto power, not a dangerous-person case. DOI: https://doi.org/10.9707/0739-1250.1493

article_title: Validation in the Shaker Era of Manifestations: A Process Analysis
author: Glendyne Wergland
page_locator: PDF pp. 5-6 and 11-16; printed pp. 124-125 and 130-135
evidence_type: historical process analysis using Shaker journals and visitor accounts
exact_factual_observation: Leaders treated separately reported matching visions as corroboration, then sent Isaac Newton Youngs to place obstacles in the girls' path and test them. Youngs was already a committed believer; after validating the visions he demonstrated their actions to leaders and peers, potentially supplying a script. A skeptical journal keeper was replaced. When a girl admitted augmenting a gift, the deception was said to have been exposed and reproved by a true gift. Doubt was veiled, questioning was discouraged to preserve union, contradictory gifts emerged, and leaders later restricted manifestations and closed public worship.
what_source_establishes: Multiple reports and an apparently empirical test are not independent when investigators, witnesses, vocabulary, incentives, and final authority share the same prior commitment. Punishing criticism and using the disputed channel to validate itself weakens falsification.

author_interpretation: The author models the episode as a multi-stage social validation process in which official acceptance enabled spread and later required regulation.
alternative_interpretation: Shared belief does not itself make an experience false; leaders did test claims, expose at least some pretense, and eventually narrow disruptive public behavior.
response_process: Separate reports; insider testing; demonstration; leadership validation; criticism suppression; insider policing of fraud; later restrictions and closure to outsiders.
outcome: The manifestations spread, generated contradictions and control problems, and were eventually constrained; public worship later became more moderate.
transferability: High for evidence-channel independence, blinded or outside assessment, preservation of dissent, and avoiding circular validation in allegations or safety reviews.
likely_article_destination: Evidence protocol / dissent / safety proxies
notes: The girl's admitted embellishment is not a dangerous-child case. DOI: https://doi.org/10.9707/0739-1250.1504

article_title: The Outlaws of Kalalau, the Aloha Spirit, and Threats to the Commune
author: Jeffrey S. Rasley
page_locator: PDF pp. 5-6 and 8-11; printed pp. 170-171 and 173-176
evidence_type: small first-person observational account with follow-up conversations and email

Member Akamai announced that thirty young Hawaiians willing to resist state authority would come to clear sacred sites. He later wrote that only Hawaiians could live in the community he intended to establish and the current Outlaws would be visitors. Chaz relied on an informal understanding and then dismissed the plan as impractical. A court jailed Akamai for camping violations and failure to appear; the proposed replacement community had not materialized by the author's next visit.

what_source_does_not_establish: It does not show that the announced group existed, that violence or displacement was imminent, that Akamai had practical control, that other members were intimidated, or that the park prosecution addressed the internal capture proposal.

notes: Tiny, informal group and a first-person account; the state action was not an internal safety remedy. DOI: https://doi.org/10.9707/0739-1250.1506

article_title: Utopian Communal Experiments in Tasmania: A Litany of Failure?
author: William Metcalf
evidence_type: historical synthesis using prospectus, press reports, official inspection, and site research
exact_factual_observation: An outside Ladies Committee controlled finances, selected members, appointed the manager, and imposed forty-one rules. Residents then faced poor soil, inadequate food, exposed housing, an allegedly incompetent manager, intrusive rules, and interpersonal conflict. article_title: Waco and Oneida: The Impact of Public Opinion on the Survival of Unconventional Religious-Communal Groups in America
author: Lawrence Foster
evidence_type: interpretive historical synthesis using a published compilation of primary Oneida sources
exact_factual_observation: After Henry Seymour severely whipped his mentally disturbed wife Tryphena, her father obtained an assault-and-battery indictment and nine members were required to testify. A settlement ended the charge: the community paid asylum expenses and promised an annual stipend after discharge. When the family later threatened additional indictments, Oneida hosted neighbors and paid the complainant for a discharge and, conditionally, for using his influence to stop the indictments. The community resumed complex marriage. The article describes no internal discipline or assessment of Seymour.
what_source_establishes: An external complaint produced treatment support and material provision that the internal system had not supplied. Conciliation can reduce escalation while also redirecting attention from offender accountability to institutional survival and suppression of further legal scrutiny.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not show that the settlement was unfair to Tryphena, that the later indictments had merit, that Seymour faced no unreported consequences, or that litigation rather than conciliation would have produced a better outcome.

alternative_interpretation: Avoiding a public trial may have protected Tryphena and secured care; the payment could be ordinary settlement rather than improper suppression. The absent internal accountability record remains material either way.
response_process: Family complaint and criminal indictment; witness testimony; out-of-court treatment and stipend agreement; later public outreach; payment conditioned on discharge and efforts to stop further indictments; no internal offender review described.
outcome: Charges were defused, the community resumed its practices and survived for decades, while the source records support for Tryphena but no stated consequence for the person who whipped her.

community_group: United Society of Believers / Shakers; Chapman family

author: Olive Jones
community_group: Renaissance, Riverside, Tui, and Wilderland communities
